newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia imposes new airport, air traffic charges.
newsitem.headline: Russia imposes new airport, air traffic charges.

text.p: Russia's Federal aviation service (FAS) will impose new airport and air traffic charges for foreign airlines flying to Russia from April 1, the state agency said on Friday.

Charges for using an airport's equipment and runway was fixed at $9.10 for each tonne of an aircraft's maximum takeoff weight, an FAS statement said. It said this charge would increase 20 percent between 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
The charge for a stopover was fixed at 10 percent of the airport's equipment and runway charge for 24 hours, but a stopover of less then three hours was free.

The FAS statement also said air traffic service during takeoff and landing would cost $3.90 for each tonne of an aircraft's maximum takeoff weight. This sum would rise 20 percent between 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. local time.

The FAS statement said foreign airlines do not have to pay air traffic service charges if their planes make flights to rescue people or aircraft, if they have technical problems during the flight or are operating training and test flights.
FAS also fixed an airport charge of $11 for each passenger who departs from Russia, excluding transit passengers.
